name: CA-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Post-redistricting fundamentals strongly favor Democrats (PVI D+7, favorable environment)
Polymarket prices a Democratic win at ~97%
Republican incumbent Gallagher runs, but incumbency edge is small in a redrawn seat
No general-election polls or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The quantitative baseline points firmly to Safe D on post-redistricting fundamentals, and prediction markets agree at roughly 97% for the Democrat. Incumbent Gallagher's presence and his fundraising edge are real but insufficient to move the forecast materially.
model.watch: Any credible general-election polling showing Gallagher running close, or heavy outside spending on his behalf, would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 1st district was redrawn to lean Democratic, and the baseline model's fundamentals point clearly in that direction, combining a D+7 partisan lean with a favorable national environment. Republican incumbent James Gallagher is running for reelection, which gives his party a modest incumbency benefit, but the model treats that as small relative to the structural shift in the seat.

There are no public general-election polls and no expert ratings for this race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals and prediction markets. Polymarket prices a Democratic win at about 97%, consistent with the baseline's Safe D call. McGuire has outraised Gallagher and enjoys outside support, though cash on hand favors the incumbent. The forecast stays at the baseline: a Democratic margin near 17 points with wide uncertainty.
